source.title: Can ChatGPT Detect Intent? Evaluating Large Language Models for Spoken Language Understanding

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present; some table formatting is flattened, but the model and score layouts are recoverable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates downstream intent-classification accuracy across language models of different sizes, a different measure from pretraining loss and the original scaling-law method.
record.gate_note: The study does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit loss power laws, test extrapolation, or investigate compute-optimal allocation or architecture-shape effects. It cites Kaplan et al. but those cited results are not rows. Rows below cover its own downstream accuracy results across differently sized models; results that vary only the number of examples for a single model are retained as conditions in that size comparison.
record.test_reason: The paper compares prompted intent-classification accuracy on SLURP across models from 774M to about 175B parameters. That bears on V6 in a new setting, though model family, instruction tuning and prompting are confounded with size.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors explicitly frame the result as an emergent ability unique to the largest models: smaller models fall far behind and fail zero-shot entirely. They identify model size as the most critical factor, with in-context examples mattering more for smaller models. They also report weak slot filling and sensitivity to ASR errors.
record.recipe_differences: Prompted downstream intent classification compared across available model sizes, rather than controlled language-model training runs and held-out pretraining-loss fitting.
record.method_sensitivity: Model size and number of in-context examples; the paper notes that longer prompts can reduce ChatGPT accuracy.
record.problems: The size comparisons use different model families and prompting setups rather than controlled runs of one family; no pretraining-loss values or uncertainty estimates are reported. The reported downstream results therefore do not establish a general scaling relationship or predict performance from loss.
record.rows_left_out: No additional size-varying downstream accuracy results are reported outside Tables 1 and 2. Other evaluations, including MINDS-14, slot filling, and ASR-transcript results, do not vary model size in a way that tests V6.

untested.parts: Prediction from pretraining loss; fitted scaling curves; any extrapolation of task accuracy to larger models; controlled single-family comparison spanning 175B.

record.verdict_notes: The comparisons mix families (GPT2, OPT, GPT3.5, ChatGPT), tuning (instruction/RLHF) and prompting setups (logit bias, beam search, batched chat). Davinci and Curie sizes are third-party estimates, and ChatGPT's size is unstated. Curie at ~6.7B far underperforms OPT-6.7B, which shows that size alone does not predict accuracy here. The 'emergent' framing means the small-model trend would not have predicted the 175B result.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss scaling with parameters, tokens, or compute.
Prediction of much larger runs from power laws fitted on smaller runs.
Effects of depth, width, and other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
Power-law scaling in other modalities or training regimes.
The study measures intent-classification accuracy, not pretraining loss; it does not test loss-to-task prediction or give a general scaling curve across controlled model families.
Dependence of fitted loss exponents or compute-optimal splits on setup and fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Few-shot (20–30 examples) prompting within the OPT family, and smaller models versus the 175B-class GPT3.5 davinci
relationships.reason: OPT accuracy rises with size at 20 and 30 examples (r26,r27,r30,r31,r34,r35), and davinci reaches 73–78% (r1–r8).
relationships.display_finding: OPT accuracy increased with size using 20 or 30 examples, while davinci reached 73–78% accuracy.

relationships.reason: Zero-shot accuracy is flat or falling from 774M to 6.7B, then jumps at 175B; authors call this emergent rather than gradual (r21,r24,r28,r32,r29,r33).
relationships.display_finding: Zero-shot accuracy was flat or falling from 774M to 6.7B before jumping at 175B, which the authors described as emergent.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: SLURP intent classification; larger GPT3.5 and ChatGPT models versus smaller Curie, GPT2, and OPT models in prompted settings
reader_labels.reason: The large GPT3.5 and ChatGPT systems obtain substantially higher accuracies than the smaller models in the reported evaluations (r1-r16, r21-r35).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Smaller models on SLURP intent classification, especially zero-shot and across example-count settings
reader_labels.reason: The smaller models have low zero-shot scores, OPT size comparisons are not consistently monotonic, and increasing examples does not uniformly raise accuracy (r9-r12, r16, r20-r24, r27-r30, r32-r33).
